catalog_entry.label: NHL draft selections (top pick and draft slot)
catalog_entry.target: Whether a named prospect is selected at an exact overall slot, or within the top N overall slots, of the NHL Draft; determined by lottery and playoff-based draft order, pick ownership and sequential club choices.
catalog_entry.mechanism: Draft order comes from two institutional pieces: slots 1-16 from the standings-weighted lottery among non-playoff clubs, slots 17-32 from playoff results, then pick ownership maps each slot to a club. Clubs choose sequentially from a shrinking board, so whether a named prospect lands at slot k depends on who was taken at slots 1..k-1; consensus is tight at the top and loose mid-round, where club need, general-manager habit, medical flags and late trades decide. Kalshi settles on the player and the overall slot, not on the club.

inputs.why: The lottery odds by final standing and ownership fix who owns each slot and the probability of moving up before selection.
Which club actually holds each first-round slot after trades, protections and forfeitures decides which team can select.
Rank-averaged public board plus its historical slot-agreement calibration is the prior over which prospect goes at each slot.
Cross-service disagreement about a prospect widens the distribution of the slot at which he is taken, beyond what the consensus gap alone implies.
Positional and pipeline need breaks ties between near-equal prospects at flat parts of the board.
A club's history of reaching for or following consensus changes how its pick is distributed.
A traded pick changes which club's preferences apply at a slot, and so which prospect is taken there, even though settlement is on the player.
Eligibility, medical and signing-path flags explain slides from the consensus rank.
The pre-lottery distribution of final standings determines the pool of lottery teams and their odds before the lottery is run.
Draft-week reports of a club's intentions are the main late signal on the top picks, and their reliability varies by source.
Lottery date, combine and draft day set when each information source arrives and when the contract can resolve.
Roster, coaching and front-office news changes club needs and may signal trades of picks before draft day.
Playoff clubs hold slots 17-32, ordered by playoff results, so slot contracts above 16 or top-N ladders with N>16 need the playoff-elimination order.
The set of prospects still available at slot k after slots 1..k-1 is the conditioning state that every exact-slot and top-N probability depends on.
League-adjusted scoring and combine testing explain where clubs deviate from the public consensus in the middle of round one.

interactions.hypothesis: A gap in mean consensus rank translates into a confident slot only when the services agree on each prospect; the same mean gap with high cross-service disagreement gives a much flatter slot distribution.

The probability a club selects at a slot is the lottery probability of that slot times the chance the club still owns the pick after protections resolve; protections only bind for specific lottery outcomes, so ownership and draw outcomes are jointly distributed, not independent.

Club need only decides the pick when the board is flat around the slot; below a dispersion threshold the consensus pick is taken regardless of need, so the need effect switches on at mid-first-round slots and is absent at the top.

A reach-prone general manager makes insider reports of an off-board choice more credible, and a consensus-following manager makes them less credible; credibility of the report and the club's historical reaching multiply rather than add.
Need acts only on the prospects left on the board: an early off-consensus pick removes a name and moves every later club's need-weighted choice, so need effects propagate down the order.

contract.settlement_definition: Settlement is on the named prospect and the overall slot, not on a club. KXNHLDRAFTPICK resolves YES only if the named player is taken at exactly the stated overall pick of the 2026 NHL Draft; KXNHLDRAFTTOP resolves YES if he is drafted anywhere within the top N overall picks (a cumulative ladder: P(top N) is non-decreasing in N). The sampled rules state nothing about the source of truth, forfeited picks, a draft postponed past expiry, or a player who goes undrafted (presumably NO). Draft-day pick trades do not change settlement because the slot number and player are what count.

rules_evidence.quote: If Wyatt Cullen is selected as the 5th overall pick in the 2026 NHL Draft, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Exact-slot contract on a named player: YES only at overall pick 5, so being taken at 4 or 6 is NO; player basis, not club basis.

rules_evidence.quote: If Malte Gustafsson is drafted top 10 in the 2026 NHL Draft, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Cumulative top-N threshold on a named player: any overall slot 1-10 settles YES, so rungs for different N are nested events.

variants_and_edge_cases: Exact slot (KXNHLDRAFTPICK, strike_type custom, e.g. 5th) versus cumulative top N (KXNHLDRAFTTOP, e.g. top 10): the first needs the full slot pmf of the player, the second its CDF at N.

Forfeited picks: when a first-round pick is forfeited (e.g. Arizona's 2021 #11) later clubs move up and the overall numbering shifts; whether 'Nth overall' refers to the announced ordinal is not stated in the rules.
Pick traded before or during the draft: settlement is unaffected (player + overall slot), but the club whose preferences apply at that slot changes, which moves probabilities.

Decentralised draft format (2025 onward, clubs picking from home markets) changes timing of announcements but not the slot definition; a postponed draft or unlisted strikes for slots above 16 are not covered by the sampled rules.

A selection later voided, or rights later renounced, should not matter because the rules key on being 'selected'/'drafted'; no rules text confirms treatment of an invalid selection reversed on the floor.
contract.settlement_data_source: Not stated in the sampled rules; presumably the NHL's official draft results (NHL.com draft tracker). Treated as unresolved.

mechanism.summary: A draft-slot contract on a named prospect is the end of a sequential chain. Slots 1-16 belong to the non-playoff clubs in reverse standings order, reshuffled by a two-draw weighted lottery (maximum rise of 10 places, no club winning more than twice in five years); slots 17-32 belong to playoff clubs, set by how far each went in the playoffs. Trades, protections and forfeitures map each slot to a holding club. Public services and club staff form boards; each holder chooses from whatever is left, so the probability the prospect goes exactly at slot k equals P(still available at k) times P(chosen | available, holder at k), and top-N is the cumulative sum over k<=N. The chain is institutional, sharp at the top of the board and diffuse mid-round, and information arrives in jumps (lottery night, combine, draft week).

stages.name: Standings and playoff results set the pre-lottery order
stages.description: Non-playoff clubs (16 of 32) hold slots 1-16 in inverse order of regular-season points percentage and tiebreakers, which also fixes their lottery odds. Playoff clubs keep their own picks and hold slots 17-32: conference-final losers pick 29-30, the Cup finalist 31 and the winner 32, with first- and second-round losers ordered by regular-season points under a rule whose division-winner detail is unverified (d5). Before the season ends this stage is a season and playoff simulation; afterwards it is deterministic.
stages.distribution: Discrete permutation of 32 clubs; slots 1-16 fixed at season end, slots 17-32 fixed only as playoff rounds finish.

stages.name: Lottery draws and ownership assignment
stages.description: The lottery holds two weighted draws among the 16 non-playoff clubs; a winner may rise at most 10 places, and the remaining lottery clubs fall in standings order. After the draws, pick ownership (trades, top-N protections, conditional swaps, forfeitures) assigns each slot to a holding club; protections resolve only once the lottery result is known, so the draw and ownership are joint.
stages.distribution: Weighted random draw without replacement; only top slots random, remaining slots a deterministic order with ownership overlay.

stages.name: Prospect board formation and consensus
stages.description: Scouting services and club staff rank the eligible prospects. The public board is summarised by mean consensus rank, the agreement among services on each prospect, and league-adjusted production and combine testing that clubs weigh differently from the services. Eligibility, injuries and signing paths demote some players. Agreement is high at the top and low across slots 8-25.
stages.distribution: Ranked order with slot-dependent dispersion; tight at the top, wide in the middle and late first round.

stages.name: Club decision rule: board, need and staff style
stages.description: Each holding club chooses from the remaining board using its own ranking (partly consensus, partly staff-specific preferences), roster and pipeline need, and an appetite for risk. Between close prospects need and staff habit decide; at the top the choice is nearly forced by consensus. Clubs also decide whether to trade the pick or trade up, which changes the selecting club.
stages.distribution: Categorical choice over the remaining board; concentrated at slot 1-3, spread across 3-8 names in the middle of round one.

stages.name: Sequential depletion of the board and ladder settlement
stages.description: Picks are made in order, so the choice at slot k is a conditional choice over prospects not taken at 1..k-1. One off-consensus pick early shifts every later slot by one name. The exact-slot contract therefore needs the joint path of the first k picks, simulated (e.g. Plackett-Luce or conditional logit over the remaining board with club-specific utilities), and the top-N contract is the cumulative availability-and-choice probability summed over slots 1..N, monotone in N.
stages.distribution: Joint categorical path over the first k slots; the named prospect's slot pmf is unimodal near consensus rank with a long right tail of slides.

stages.name: Late information and announcement
stages.description: In draft week insider reports, combine medicals and trade rumours move the likelihood of particular selections in jumps; the outcome settles when the pick is announced at the draft. The sampled rules settle on the player selected at an overall slot, so post-selection trades of the player do not matter, while a pre-selection trade of the pick changes which club's board applies.
stages.distribution: Binary resolution after a discrete announcement; late reports shift probabilities in jumps, not smoothly.

talent_strength.note: Prospect quality enters as the public consensus order and league-adjusted production; not on-ice performance of the selecting club.

opponent_matchup.note: There is no opponent in a draft selection; the only interaction is between the holding club's needs and the remaining board, handled under role_personnel.

role_personnel.note: Club needs and decision-maker habits determine the selection among close prospects.

availability_news.note: Medical, eligibility and draft-week reporting change who is available at a slot.

coaching_scheme.note: On-ice coaching tactics do not decide draft choices; the relevant staff effect is the general manager and scouting director behaviour captured in gm_draft_behavior_history.

environment.note: Venue, weather and travel have no bearing on a draft selection made at a league event; no environmental variable alters the outcome.

game_context_script.note: No game is played; there is no score state, pace or overtime. The comparable timeline structure is the lottery-then-draft sequence in the calendar.

pace_volume.note: No count of events accumulates; the outcome is one selection per slot, not a volume of shots, possessions or plays over a window.

efficiency_conversion.note: No conversion rate generates the outcome; how often consensus translates into the actual pick is a calibration held in prospect_consensus_ranking.

distribution_variance.note: Cross-service disagreement and the sequential-depletion path set the width and right tail of the prospect's slot pmf.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Standings stakes determine the pool, and the timeline of lottery and draft day sets when trades and information arrive.

officiating_rules.note: League lottery rules (two draws, max rise 10, two wins in five years), the playoff-slot ordering rule and pick-ownership rules govern the process.

settlement_contract.note: Rules settle on player + overall slot (exact or top N); the slot pmf/CDF from the board path maps directly to both. Source of truth and forfeiture numbering unresolved (d1).

nhl.draft_team_need_profile.label: Club organisational need profile at the pick (positions, prospect pipeline depth, window)
nhl.draft_team_need_profile.mechanism: Translates a club's current roster, prospect pool and competitive window into position and archetype preferences when two or more prospects are close on the board.
nhl.draft_team_need_profile.rationale: Early picks are mostly decided by consensus, but between near-tied prospects clubs lean toward centre/defence scarcity or toward a pipeline gap. The subtlety is that NHL clubs historically claim to take best available, so the need effect is small at the top and grows only where the board is flat.
nhl.draft_team_need_profile.measurement: For each club holding a first-round pick compute, as of draft week, (a) count and quality (draft-pedigree-weighted) of signed or drafted prospects aged <=22 by position C/W/D/G, (b) NHL roster age and contract-expiry profile by position over the next 3 seasons, (c) rebuild-vs-contend flag from last-two-season points%. Express as a position-need z-score vs league mean; shrink to zero with k=3 historical picks per club-position cell to avoid noise; freeze at the draft-order-final timestamp.
free_sources: Elite Prospects team prospect pools (free tier)
PuckPedia contract tables (CapFriendly closed in 2024; Wayback snapshots only)
raw_data: club prospect pool table: player, position, age, draft slot
nhl.draft_team_need_profile.why: Differentiates which of two close prospects a particular club takes at a specific slot, and so which club ends up with the contested player.

nhl.draft_board_dispersion.label: Cross-service disagreement on each prospect's rank
nhl.draft_board_dispersion.mechanism: Measures how much independent services disagree about one prospect, which is information the mean consensus rank and the rank-1 vs rank-2 gap (held in prospect_consensus_ranking) do not carry.
nhl.draft_board_dispersion.rationale: Two prospects with the same mean rank can have SD 0.5 or SD 6 across services; the second is far more likely to be taken well away from his mean. This input is only the disagreement measure; the slot calibration lives in prospect_consensus_ranking, so it is not counted twice.
nhl.draft_board_dispersion.measurement: For each prospect at the as-of date take ranks from every service available for that year (NHL Central Scouting split NA/EU lists mapped to a combined rank, TSN/McKenzie, Elite Prospects public list, others where archived; minimum 3), compute the cross-service SD of rank and the inter-quartile range, winsorise ranks at 64. No slot calibration here; used as a covariate in the conditional-logit utility. History limited to years with >=3 archived services (expected ~2012 onward; see d6).
free_sources: TSN/Bob McKenzie final rankings (public pages, patchy before ~2010)
raw_data: service ranks by prospect and publication date
nhl.draft_board_dispersion.why: Widens or narrows the named prospect's slot distribution for exact-slot and top-N contracts.

nhl.draft_pick_trade_hazard.label: Probability a held pick changes club or slot before selection
nhl.draft_pick_trade_hazard.mechanism: Estimates the chance the slot is traded to another club (or the selection traded post-pick) between the lottery and the selection call, changing which club makes the pick.
nhl.draft_pick_trade_hazard.rationale: Contracts that settle on which team selects, rather than which player, depend on pick ownership at the moment the pick is announced. Picks are frequently moved on draft day, and top-3 picks move rarely but non-zero, so a static ownership table is not a final answer.
nhl.draft_pick_trade_hazard.measurement: From the draft-pick transaction history 2005-present compute, per slot bucket (1-3, 4-10, 11-20, 21-32), the share of picks that changed club within the 14 days before selection and on draft day, separated by whether the holding club is a seller or buyer by points% rank. Add a club-level multiplier from past count of draft-day trades per GM, shrunk to league with k=4 drafts. As-of the ownership table timestamp. Settlement is on the player, so the hazard enters only by switching which club's utility applies at the slot.
raw_data: pick transaction log with date, from-club, to-club, slot
nhl.draft_pick_trade_hazard.why: A pick changing hands swaps the club whose need and habits apply at that slot, moving the named prospect's slot probability.

nhl.prospect_eligibility_medical_flags.label: Prospect eligibility, signing-rights and medical availability flags
nhl.prospect_eligibility_medical_flags.mechanism: Captures whether each prospect is eligible for the given draft, has no contractual or injury obstacle to being taken at a high slot.
nhl.prospect_eligibility_medical_flags.rationale: A top prospect with a major injury, an age-eligibility edge case, or a contract-rights complication can slide by several slots. The slide is asymmetric: clubs seldom move a prospect up for reasons of health.
nhl.prospect_eligibility_medical_flags.measurement: For each of the top-40 prospects as-of the draft combine and the week before the draft, record binary or ordinal flags: eligible (born by the cut-off date), over-ager status, injury within last 12 months with games missed share, combine medical concerns reported, and signing-path complexity (CHL vs NCAA vs European contract). Convert to an expected slot slide in positions via a regression on historical prospects with the same flag class, shrunk with k=10 prospects per class.
nhl.prospect_eligibility_medical_flags.why: Moves probability mass off a prospect whose slot is being priced, and onto the next name on the board.

nhl.gm_draft_behavior_history.label: General-manager and scouting-staff draft behaviour history
nhl.gm_draft_behavior_history.mechanism: Learns how often a club's decision-makers deviate from the consensus board and in which direction (upside, size, age, nationality) from their past selections.
nhl.gm_draft_behavior_history.rationale: A club that has repeatedly reached for specific archetypes makes a different pick than the board implies; consensus-following clubs follow the board. The GM and head scout identity matters because staff turnover resets the habit.
nhl.gm_draft_behavior_history.measurement: Over the last 8 drafts, per club-staff regime compute (a) mean signed difference between actual slot and consensus rank, (b) share of first-round picks that were outside the consensus top-N for that slot, (c) preference weights for size/age/league by regression on the consensus residual. Shrink to league with k=6 picks, reset on a change of GM or director of amateur scouting, and apply only to the slot where the club selects.
raw_data: draft picks by club: slot, consensus rank
nhl.gm_draft_behavior_history.why: Turns the board into a club-specific selection distribution when the contract settles on a named club's pick.

nhl.draft_order_playoff_elimination.label: Draft order of playoff clubs (slots 17-32) from round of elimination and regular-season points
nhl.draft_order_playoff_elimination.mechanism: Assigns slots 17-32 to the 16 playoff clubs from how far each advanced and from regular-season points within groups, so it depends on playoff series outcomes.
nhl.draft_order_playoff_elimination.rationale: Before the playoffs end, which club picks at 17-32 is uncertain; a prospect projected in the 20s is more likely to go to a club whose board or need suits him. Cup winner 32, finalist 31 and conference-final losers 29-30 are firm; the ordering of earlier losers (pure points vs division-winner adjustment) must be checked against the current rule (d5).
nhl.draft_order_playoff_elimination.measurement: Simulate the bracket from nhl.bracket_path_difficulty and per-series win probabilities from ratings with posterior uncertainty (10,000 paths); for each path apply the league's slot rule to produce a 17-32 order; report P(club holds slot k) for k=17..32. After each round, condition on eliminated clubs. As-of: the latest completed series.
free_sources: NHL.com playoff results and draft-order pages
nhl.draft_order_playoff_elimination.why: Needed for exact-slot contracts above 16 and top-N ladders with N>16, which depend on which club picks in the 20s.

nhl.draft_remaining_board_state.label: [Model state, joint simulation] Prospects still available at slot k given picks 1..k-1
nhl.draft_remaining_board_state.mechanism: Simulates the draft pick by pick: each holder chooses among the remaining prospects, so availability at slot k is the result of all earlier choices.
nhl.draft_remaining_board_state.rationale: Calibrating on the unconditional 'rank-k prospect went at slot k' is wrong once an early reach happens, since one off-board pick shifts every later slot. The quantity the contracts need, P(prospect at k) and P(prospect by N), only exists as a joint path probability.
nhl.draft_remaining_board_state.measurement: Conditional logit (or Plackett-Luce) over the remaining top-64 board at each slot: utility = b1*consensus mean rank + b2*cross-service SD + b3*need match + b4*club reach tendency + b5*production/combine residual + medical flag, with club-staff random effects shrunk to league (k=6 picks). Fit on drafts with archived boards (~2012 onward, d6), validate by log-loss of actual picks 1-32. Simulate 20,000 draft paths with ownership and lottery draws; output each prospect's slot pmf and CDF.
free_sources: Derived from the public ranking archive, ownership log and club profiles in required_data
raw_data: full top-64 board by service and date
ownership by slot at draft time
nhl.draft_remaining_board_state.why: Produces the exact-slot pmf and top-N CDF that the two Kalshi series settle on.

nhl.prospect_production_profile.label: Prospect league-adjusted production and combine testing
nhl.prospect_production_profile.mechanism: Translates junior, NCAA and European scoring into an NHL-equivalent rate and records combine fitness results, the evidence clubs weigh when they leave the consensus.
nhl.prospect_production_profile.rationale: Consensus rankings absorb production, which suffices at slot 1, but mid-round deviations by clubs correlate with points per game, age-adjusted, and size/skating; the residual of production versus consensus rank is what helps predict a reach or a slide.
nhl.prospect_production_profile.measurement: Draft-year points per game by league, converted with NHLe league factors (published translation factors, re-estimated on 10 seasons of players moving between leagues), adjusted for age at 15 September of the draft year (birth-month effect) and position; combine fitness percentiles where released. Store as residual versus consensus rank, as of draft week.
nhl.prospect_production_profile.why: Explains which prospects a club takes ahead of or behind consensus at the named slot.

nhl.draft_lottery_odds_by_standing.reason: Directly generates the slot-ownership order: odds are fixed by pre-lottery standing and the lottery draw is the only random step upstream of club choices.

nhl.pick_ownership_and_protection.reason: Needed to map a slot to the club that selects; pick protections and conditional swaps change the holder and are written down before the draft.

nhl.prospect_consensus_ranking.reason: Best public prior; its catalog definition already holds the rank-1/rank-2 gap and the historical slot-agreement calibration, so the separate dispersion input is narrowed to cross-service disagreement and reference_class_hazard was removed as a third copy.

nhl.season_sim_distribution.reason: Useful only before the season ends, to price lottery-pool membership; once the lottery is run it adds nothing, so it is a time-limited input.

nhl.insider_report_credibility.reason: Draft-week insider claims about the first pick are the main late information; credibility and lag weighting is what stops reports from being over- or under-weighted.

nhl.announcement_calendar.reason: Gives the timeline (lottery, combine, draft day) that determines when information resolves; does not move the probability itself.

nhl.news.reason: Generic transactions feed; relevant mainly for front-office changes and pick trades, otherwise noisy for draft slots.

interactions.mechanism: The consensus mean-rank gap between two prospects predicts their relative slots well only when services agree on each; with high cross-service disagreement the same mean gap carries little information and the slot distribution flattens.
interactions.how_to_test: Conditional logit with consensus gap, cross-service SD and their product as covariates; test the product term by held-out log-loss on drafts ~2012-present, split slot 1-3 vs 4-32.

interactions.mechanism: The probability a club selects at a slot is the lottery probability of that slot times the chance the club still owns the pick after protections resolve; protections only bind for specific lottery outcomes, so ownership and draw outcomes are jointly distributed, not independent.
interactions.how_to_test: Enumerate lottery draw outcomes for a historical year with a protected pick and compare the marginal-by-product probability vs the joint enumeration of draw-and-protection outcomes.

interactions.mechanism: Club need only decides the pick when the board is flat around the slot; below a dispersion threshold the consensus pick is taken regardless of need, so the need effect switches on at mid-first-round slots and is absent at the top.
interactions.how_to_test: Add need x flatness interaction and test whether the need coefficient is zero for slots 1-3 and positive for slots 8-20 in a conditional logit over remaining prospects.

interactions.mechanism: A reach-prone general manager makes insider reports of an off-board choice more credible, and a consensus-following manager makes them less credible; credibility of the report and the club's historical reaching multiply rather than add. Untestable until insider reports are captured over several drafts (d7).
interactions.how_to_test: Back-test reported-pick accuracy by source for reach-prone vs consensus-following clubs and test an interaction term in the pick model.

interactions.mechanism: Before the lottery, trade hazard concerns picks of unknown slot and is low for top slots; after the lottery and especially on draft day it concentrates on known slots, so the hazard regime changes at the lottery date and again on draft day.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate pick-change frequency separately in windows before lottery, between lottery and draft day, and on draft day, and test slot x window interaction.

interactions.mechanism: Need matters only over the prospects left: if an earlier club takes the defenceman a later club needed, that club's choice moves to the next need fit, so an off-consensus pick propagates down the order and the named prospect's slot pmf shifts as a whole.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare a sequential simulation with need terms against independent slot-by-slot predictions, by log-loss of each prospect's actual slot, on drafts with one or more top-10 reaches.

nonlinearities.shape: Probability the consensus rank-k prospect goes exactly at k falls convexly with k: near 0.8-0.9 at k=1, quickly below 0.3 by k=5-10
nonlinearities.why: Historical agreement between consensus and actual slot is high only at the very top; a linear rank effect overstates mid-round confidence for exact-slot contracts.

nonlinearities.shape: Odds of winning a draw are concentrated in the worst few clubs and capped by the 10-place rise limit
nonlinearities.why: The published odds are not proportional to standing; the two draws and movement cap make the mapping from points rank to slot piecewise.

nonlinearities.shape: Need effect saturates: beyond a modest positional deficit extra need adds little because clubs rarely reach more than a few slots
nonlinearities.why: Clubs trade need off against board value; a large need does not translate into proportionally larger reach, so the effect is bounded.

nonlinearities.shape: Top-N probability is a CDF in N: flat near 0 until slots where the prospect becomes available, steep near consensus rank, then saturating
nonlinearities.why: Top-N rungs are nested; P(by N) must be non-decreasing in N and the exact-slot pmf is its first difference, so ladder rungs must be priced from one joint simulation.

unresolved.description: Sampled rules for KXNHLDRAFTPICK and KXNHLDRAFTTOP give only the YES condition; they do not name a source of truth, say whether 'Nth overall' counts forfeited slots, or say what happens if the draft is postponed past expiry or a selection is ruled invalid.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Read the full Kalshi rulebook/terms page for these series or a disputed-settlement notice covering forfeits and postponement.

unresolved.description: Current lottery mechanics (number of draws, maximum positions a club can rise, any limit on repeated wins) are quoted from general knowledge and may have changed since the last rule revision.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Read the league's current lottery procedure page and confirm each rule against the most recent lottery results.

unresolved.description: Clubs' internal draft boards and need rankings are private; public rankings are the only board proxy, so club-specific preferences are inferred from past picks only.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Compare out-of-sample accuracy of the inferred club preferences against actual picks over several drafts.

unresolved.description: Effect of the need profile versus best-available is contested in public work and may be near zero in the top five; its size by slot band is not established.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Estimate the need coefficient by slot band on historical drafts and test whether it is distinguishable from zero.

unresolved.description: The exact current rule ordering playoff clubs in slots 17-28 (pure regular-season points versus a division-winner adjustment) is from memory; only slots 29-32 (conference-final losers, finalist, winner) are certain.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Read the NHL's current draft-order procedure and check it against the 2024-2026 first-round orders.

unresolved.description: A multi-service public ranking history back to 2005 probably does not exist: McKeen's and FC Hockey are paywalled, the Elite Prospects draft guide is paid, McKenzie archives are patchy before about 2010. Calibration windows for the board model may be limited to ~2012 onward.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Inventory archived final rankings per service per year and fix the calibration window to years with at least three services.

unresolved.description: Draft-week insider reports have no clean public archive, so insider_report_credibility and its interaction with GM reach tendency cannot be back-tested until the project captures reports across several drafts.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Capture timestamped insider claims for at least three drafts and score them against actual picks.

unresolved.description: CapFriendly, the main free historical source for pick conditions and protections, shut down in July 2024; completeness of PuckPedia and Wayback snapshots for 2005-2024 pick conditions is unchecked.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Sample 30 conditional picks from 2010-2024 and check whether PuckPedia or Wayback snapshots record their conditions and resolution.

catalog_entry.label: NHL playoff series aggregate outcomes (series total goals, length, exact score, game spread, OT count, 3-0 comeback)
catalog_entry.target: A quantity defined over a whole best-of-7 playoff series (total goals, games played, exact winner-and-length score, margin in games, count of overtime games), or a path event across all series of one postseason (any 0-3 comeback). Each depends on the joint distribution of the winner and length (4-7 games) and, for goals and OT, on per-game scoring and ties.
catalog_entry.mechanism: Per-game win probabilities from team ratings (with shared posterior uncertainty), goaltending and the 2-2-1-1-1 home pattern give the joint winner-by-length pmf that settles series games, exact score, game spread and championship score. Series total goals add per-game scoring, lowered by the playoff environment and shifted by series state, with every regulation tie adding exactly one sudden-death goal. The OT-game count uses regulation-tie probability with within-series dependence. The league-wide 0-3 comeback event aggregates the path probability over the bracket.

inputs.why: Live series state (score, games played, home ice, rest, lineup) determines how many games remain and the goals already banked.
Model output, not data: the joint winner-by-length pmf computed from ratings, goalies, venue and the dependence parameter; it maps directly to games, score and spread settlement.
Team strength gap determines per-game win probability and so series length and, through goal means, per-game scoring.
The goaltender is the largest controllable driver of both goals against and series length in the playoffs.
Per-game goal totals are overdispersed with home-away correlation; the series sum inherits that dispersion.
Playoff scoring runs lower than the regular season with fewer penalties and continuous overtime; this fixes the per-game goal mean.
Trailing, elimination and game-seven states shift the per-game goal rate in ways the series score reveals.
Adjustments across the series change scoring by game index, which matters for later games in a long series.
Shot-quality creation sets team goal means with less noise than raw goals.
Shot-quality suppression sets the opponent's goal mean and the series total.
Goaltending variance beyond binomial changes how lopsided individual games are; the direction of its effect on length depends on which side's goalie runs hot.
Attempts per 60 for the pair controls shots and so goals, and drops in playoff matchups.
Power-play and penalty-kill matchups produce a share of playoff goals despite fewer penalties.
Penalty frequency determines power-play opportunities, a large source of variance in goals.
Injuries to stars and goalies mid-series change per-game strength and thus length and goals.
Explicit state-conditional empty-net module; dispersion is then fitted on non-empty-net goals so empty-net goals are not counted twice.
The year-level scoring level recalibrates the goal mean of every game.
Probability a game is tied after regulation decides how often a game adds exactly one OT goal and is the per-game rate for the series OT-count contract.
Beta-binomial overdispersion of OT-game counts within a series sets the tail for 'at least k games go to overtime' strikes.
Uncertainty in the pair's strength differential is shared by every game; averaging over it makes series more lopsided (shorter) and moves the winner-by-length cells.
Playoff starter changes after a bad game shift per-game goals and win probability for the remaining games of the series.
Days between playoff games vary from one to three or more, and cross-country travel within a series changes per-game strength.
Which matchups occur in later rounds drives the championship exact-score market listed before the Final and the league-wide comeback event.
Fitted sign and size of game-to-game dependence within a series; the only data-estimated quantity behind the length pmf beyond per-game probabilities.
Win probability of a team facing elimination or trailing 0-3 differs from its pre-series rate, which drives comeback and 7-game probabilities.
An error in the pair's combined scoring level is shared by every game, so series-total variance grows with games squared; the strength-differential posterior does not carry it.

interactions.hypothesis: Uncertainty about the strength gap is shared by all games: averaging the length pmf over the rating posterior lowers expected length and the game-7 share near parity.
A hot favourite goalie shortens the series and lowers goals per game (both reduce the total); a hot underdog goalie lowers goals per game but lengthens the series, so the effects on the total offset.
Empty-net goals concentrate in late one-goal deficits of elimination games, so their contribution to series goals depends on series state.

The OT-game count is a beta-binomial over games played with per-game rate from the tie model; closely matched pairs have both higher tie rates and longer series, so the count's tail rises faster than either alone.
A 0-3 comeback needs four straight wins by the trailing team; its probability depends on the trailing team's state-shifted win rate compounded by the sign of game-to-game dependence.

Shared scoring-level uncertainty adds variance proportional to games squared, so it widens total-goal tails most for evenly rated pairs that play long series and least for mismatches that end in four or five.

contract.settlement_definition: Seven series, all with rules text. KXNHLSERIESTOTALGOAL: YES if the two teams 'collectively score at least' N goals across the series (OT goals not mentioned; read as all goals). KXNHLSERIESGAMES: YES if more than 6.5 games are played (i.e. a game 7). KXNHLSERIESSCORE and KXNHLFINALSEXACT: YES on an exact winner-and-score such as 4-3. KXNHLSERIESSPREAD: YES if the named team wins by more than 2.5 games (4-0 or 4-1). KXNHLSERIESOT: YES if at least k games of the Final go to overtime. KXNHL30COMEBACK: YES if any team in the postseason wins a series after trailing 0-3. No rule states the source of truth or treatment of an unfinished series.

rules_evidence.quote: collectively score at least 50 goals, then the market resolves to Yes
rules_evidence.establishes: Threshold on combined goals across the whole series (>= N, integer strike); overtime goals are not mentioned, neither included nor excluded.

rules_evidence.quote: If above 6.5 games are played in the Vegas Golden Knights vs Carolina Hurricanes Stanley Cup series
rules_evidence.establishes: Series-length over/under at 6.5, so YES iff the series reaches game 7; depends only on the length pmf.

rules_evidence.quote: If the series score is Vegas Golden Knights wins 4-3
rules_evidence.establishes: Exact joint outcome of winner and length; one cell of the 8-cell winner-by-length pmf.

rules_evidence.quote: If Vegas Golden Knights wins by more than 2.5 games
rules_evidence.establishes: Game margin above 2.5 means the named team wins 4-0 or 4-1; sum of two pmf cells.

rules_evidence.quote: If at least 5 games go to overtime in the Vegas Golden Knights vs Carolina Hurricanes Stanley Cup
rules_evidence.establishes: Count of overtime games within one series compared with an integer strike (>=5); needs the tie rate and series length jointly.

rules_evidence.quote: they lose the first three games of a series (going down 0-3), and then win four consecutive games to win the series 4-3
rules_evidence.establishes: League-wide path event over every series of the 2026 playoffs; requires the 0-3 start and four straight wins.

rules_evidence.quote: If Florida wins 4-3 in the 2025 Pro Hockey Championship series
rules_evidence.establishes: Exact winner-and-length score for the championship series, which may list before the finalists are known.

variants_and_edge_cases: Overtime goals in KXNHLSERIESTOTALGOAL: the rule says 'collectively score', which naturally includes sudden-death OT goals (exactly one per OT game, no shootouts in the playoffs); not stated explicitly.
Markets listed mid-series: goals, games and OT games already played count toward the strike, so the model must condition on the banked state at the listing timestamp.
KXNHLFINALSEXACT and any pre-round listing: the named team may not reach the series, which then presumably settles NO; requires P(reach) times P(exact score | matchup).
KXNHL30COMEBACK aggregates up to 15 series across four rounds; a single comeback anywhere settles YES, and later-round series exist only conditionally on earlier results.

A series not completed (suspension, cancellation) and the source of truth are not addressed by any sampled rule; KXNHLSERIESTOTALGOALS (plural) appears in the ledger narrative but not in the live series of this pack.
contract.settlement_data_source: Not stated in the sampled rules; presumably official NHL game results (NHL.com / NHL API boxscores). Treated as unresolved (p1).

mechanism.summary: Every contract here is a function of one best-of-7 sequence. Per-game win probabilities from ratings, goaltending, rest and venue, with the 2-2-1-1-1 home pattern, give a joint pmf over winner and length (8 cells): games over/under, exact score, game spread and the championship score read cells directly. Uncertainty about the pair's strength is shared across games; averaging over it makes series more lopsided (shorter), not longer, while any negative game-to-game dependence would lengthen them, so the sign is empirical. Total goals are a random-length sum of overdispersed per-game totals, where each regulation tie adds exactly one sudden-death goal. The OT-game count is a dependent sum of tie indicators. The league-wide 0-3 comeback event combines path probabilities over the bracket.

stages.name: Per-game strength and goal means for the pair
stages.description: Each game's expected goals for and against come from the two teams' attack and suppression quality, the confirmed starter, special teams, rest days and the playoff scoring environment. Strength is a posterior, not a point: its uncertainty is common to all games of the series, both for the strength differential (which moves length) and for the combined scoring level (which widens the goal sum). Injuries and goalie switches during the series change the inputs for remaining games only.
stages.distribution: Poisson-like goal counts per team with overdispersion and a positive home-away correlation.

stages.name: Joint winner-by-length pmf from the game sequence
stages.description: Home and away win probabilities, the 2-2-1-1-1 home-ice pattern and any within-series dependence give P(winner, length) over 8 cells. Mixing over shared rating uncertainty spreads the effective per-game probability away from 0.5, which lowers E[length] (5.81 games at iid parity) and the game-7 share; only negative dependence such as bounce-back would raise them. The sign is estimated, not assumed. Elimination-state shifts in win probability alter the late cells.
stages.distribution: Discrete pmf over 8 winner-by-length cells; P(7 games) at most 0.3125 under iid parity and lower with heterogeneity.

stages.name: State-dependent scoring through the series
stages.description: Goals per game shift with the series score and game index: elimination games raise empty-net risk and goalie pulls, early games reflect regular-season matchups, later games reflect coaching adjustments and fatigue. The state also feeds back into length: a team trailing 0-3 produces a short series. This stage maps series trajectories to goals per game and makes the sum depend on the path.
stages.distribution: Path-dependent mixture; per-game mean shifts by a few percent by state, and the sum has covariance across games.

stages.name: Regulation ties, overtime games and the OT goal
stages.description: A playoff game tied after 60 minutes continues in 20-minute 5v5 sudden-death periods with no shootout, so it adds exactly one goal however many periods it takes, and the series total equals regulation goals plus the number of OT games. The OT-game count for the overtime contract is a sum of tie indicators over games played, with per-game rate from the regulation-tie model and within-series overdispersion; ties are more likely in closely matched pairs, which also play longer series.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli tie per game (~0.2-0.25); OT count beta-binomial given length; OT adds a deterministic +1 goal per tied game.

stages.name: Bracket and league-wide path aggregation
stages.description: The championship exact-score market can list before the finalists are known, and the 0-3 comeback event spans up to 15 series whose later-round matchups depend on earlier results. Both need a bracket simulation: P(team reaches series) from the bracket path, then the series-level path probability. A team down 0-3 is usually the weaker side, which is why the historical comeback rate (four completions: 1942 TOR, 1975 NYI, 2010 PHI, 2014 LAK) sits far below the iid parity value of 1/16.
stages.distribution: Union over series of rare path events; approximately 1 - prod(1 - p_s) with dependence through shared bracket outcomes.

stages.name: Mapping series outcomes to each contract and the banked state
stages.description: Each series reads a different functional of the simulation: total goals compares the summed goals (regulation plus one per OT game) with an integer strike, games over 6.5 is P(game 7), spread above 2.5 is P(4-0 or 4-1 for the named team), exact score is one cell, and the OT market compares the OT count with k. A market opened mid-series conditions on goals, games and OT games already banked.
stages.distribution: Deterministic functionals of the simulated path; integer strikes make each total a step function of the path.

talent_strength.note: Team and goalie quality set the goal means and the per-game win probability.

opponent_matchup.note: Pair-specific special teams and adjustments within a series; bracket path sets which pairs meet.

role_personnel.note: Availability of key skaters and who starts in goal change the pair's per-game rates.

availability_news.note: Mid-series injuries and starter changes change remaining-game strength.

coaching_scheme.note: Between-game adjustments and elimination-game tactics alter scoring by game index and state.

environment.note: Playoff environment and season scoring level set the goal mean; arena effects are small and left as context.

game_context_script.note: Regulation ties, series state, empty-net behaviour and banked state are the script of the aggregate.

pace_volume.note: Two volume scales: attempts per game and the number of games (from the length pmf, a model output).

efficiency_conversion.note: Finishing and goaltending conversion determine goals from shot volume, with regression to a team mean.

distribution_variance.note: Per-game overdispersion, shared strength-differential uncertainty (length), shared scoring-level uncertainty (total-goal variance scaling with games squared), OT-count overdispersion and game dependence.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Elimination states, rest days between games and travel inside the 2-2-1-1-1 pattern.

officiating_rules.note: Playoff crews call fewer penalties; sudden-death OT with no shootout fixes the OT goal at exactly one.

settlement_contract.note: Each series maps to a functional of the winner-length pmf, OT count or goal sum; OT goal counting for totals and source of truth unresolved (p1).

nhl.series_game_count_pmf.label: [Model output, not raw data] Joint series winner-by-length pmf (8 cells) from per-game probabilities and home-ice pattern
nhl.series_game_count_pmf.mechanism: Builds the probability that a best-of-seven ends in exactly 4, 5, 6 or 7 games from each game's win probability, with the 2-2-1-1-1 home sequence and between-game dependence.
nhl.series_game_count_pmf.rationale: Games, exact-score, spread and championship-score contracts settle directly on cells of this pmf, and total goals sum over its length. It is computed from ratings, goalies and venue, so it must not be counted as independent information next to them. Shared rating uncertainty makes series more lopsided (shorter) rather than longer; whether game-to-game dependence offsets that is estimated in series_game_dependence.
nhl.series_game_count_pmf.measurement: For each series compute home/away win probabilities from ratings drawn from the rating posterior, goalie, injuries and rest (as of the pre-series timestamp), apply series_state_win_prob_shift in elimination states and the fitted dependence from series_game_dependence, and enumerate or simulate 20,000 paths through 2-2-1-1-1 to get P(winner, length). Calibrate against 2005-06 onward series: historical game-7 share and sweep share by pre-series favourite bucket. Recompute after each game conditional on the series score.
raw_data: series results by year with game count
nhl.series_game_count_pmf.why: Supplies the winner-by-length cells used by games, score and spread settlement and the number of summed games for goals.

nhl.series_state_scoring_shift.label: Series-state effect on per-game goal rate (elimination, trailing team, game-7 intensity)
nhl.series_state_scoring_shift.mechanism: Adjusts expected goals per game for the series score, since trailing and elimination games change risk-taking, line usage, goaltending changes and empty-net frequency.
nhl.series_state_scoring_shift.rationale: A series that is 3-0 behaves differently from 1-1: the trailing team pulls goalies earlier and the leader sits back, but the state is also what lengthens or shortens the series. The effect on goals is mixed across directions, so it must be measured rather than assumed.
nhl.series_state_scoring_shift.measurement: From playoff games 2008-present tag each game by series score entering the game (e.g. 0-0, 1-0, 1-1, 2-1, 3-0, 3-1, 3-2, 3-3) and elimination flag; regress total goals per game (regulation plus OT) on state dummies, team rating-implied goal mean and venue, with a team random effect. Shrink small cells with k=15 games to the pooled mean; report multiplicative shift factors by state with standard errors.
free_sources: NHL API play-by-play and game results
raw_data: playoff game results with series score entering game
play-by-play with empty-net goals and goalie pull times
nhl.series_state_scoring_shift.why: Provides the conditional adjustment of the summed goals per game, which cannot be read from the single-game total archetype.

nhl.series_adjustment_regime.label: Coaching adjustment and matchup learning across games in a series
nhl.series_adjustment_regime.mechanism: Captures how coaches change lines, matchups, special-teams assignments and goalie decisions between games, shifting pace and goals as the series progresses.
nhl.series_adjustment_regime.rationale: Early series games are sampled with the regular-season matchup profile; later games reflect adjustments and fatigue, and the typical drift in scoring across game number is not zero. Home last-change opportunity compounds this.
nhl.series_adjustment_regime.measurement: Compute from playoff games 2010-present the average change in goals per game from game 1-2 to game 5-7 conditioning on round, and the team coach-level adjustment effect measured as residual of scoring versus rating prediction at game index k. Use a team-coach random effect with shrinkage k=20 games, windows over four seasons, and exclude games played after a goalie change from the baseline.
free_sources: NHL API play-by-play and shift charts (line combinations derived from shared shifts)
raw_data: playoff game results by game index
shift charts for line combinations, starters from boxscores
nhl.series_adjustment_regime.why: Allows scoring to drift with game index rather than assuming constant per-game goals across the series.

nhl.series_game_dependence.label: Within-series game-to-game dependence of results (sign and size)
nhl.series_game_dependence.mechanism: Estimates whether, beyond fixed per-game probabilities, the result of game g changes the win probability of game g+1 (positive: momentum; negative: bounce-back or loser-adjusts).
nhl.series_game_dependence.rationale: The two candidate mechanisms push length in opposite directions: momentum and shared strength make series shorter, bounce-back lengthens them. Treating any dependence as 'fattening the 7-game tail' gets the sign wrong for shared shocks; it must be estimated after removing the shared-strength mixing.
nhl.series_game_dependence.measurement: On playoff series 2005-06 onward, fit a logit for game g outcome with pre-series rating-implied log-odds, home flag, and lagged result of game g-1 (and series score), with the series-level rating posterior integrated out; the lag coefficient gives the dependence. Shrink toward 0 with a normal prior sd 0.15; compare the predicted game-7 and sweep shares with the observed shares as a check of sign.
raw_data: playoff game results in order with series id
nhl.series_game_dependence.why: Determines whether the length pmf should be shifted toward or away from 6-7 games relative to the mixed-iid model.

nhl.series_state_win_prob_shift.label: Series-state shift in per-game win probability (elimination, trailing 0-3 or 1-3, closeout games)
nhl.series_state_win_prob_shift.mechanism: Adjusts each team's per-game win probability for the series state entering the game, such as facing elimination or trying to close out.
nhl.series_state_win_prob_shift.rationale: The comeback contract depends on the trailing team winning four straight; teams down 0-3 are selected to be weaker, so the raw historical rate mixes selection and any genuine desperation effect. Separating the two needs the pre-series rating as a control.
nhl.series_state_win_prob_shift.measurement: From playoff games 2005-06 onward (plus 1987-2005 for the rare 0-3 states, with era flag), logit of game outcome on rating-implied log-odds, home flag and state dummies (facing elimination, closeout, 0-3, 1-3, 3-3); shrink state effects toward 0 with k=40 games per state. Report shift in log-odds by state; validate against the four completed 0-3 comebacks in NHL history and the count of 0-3 deficits.
free_sources: Hockey-Reference playoff series and game logs
raw_data: playoff game results with series score entering the game
nhl.series_state_win_prob_shift.why: Sets late-game cells of the length pmf and the per-series probability of a 0-3 comeback.

nhl.series_pair_scoring_rate_uncertainty.label: Shared posterior uncertainty in the pair's combined goal rate (attack plus defence sum) for one series
nhl.series_pair_scoring_rate_uncertainty.mechanism: Posterior SD of the matchup's expected total goals per game (both teams' attack and suppression components summed), a level error shared by every game of the series.
nhl.series_pair_scoring_rate_uncertainty.rationale: rating_posterior_uncertainty describes uncertainty in the strength differential, which moves who wins and the series length but not the combined scoring level. An error in the pair's total goal rate is common to all games, so the variance it adds to series total goals scales with the square of games played, unlike per-game overdispersion, which scales linearly. Ignoring it understates both tails of KXNHLSERIESTOTALGOAL strikes.
nhl.series_pair_scoring_rate_uncertainty.measurement: Fit a bivariate Poisson/negative-binomial team model with separate attack and defence effects on score-adjusted xG and goals (3 seasons, exponential decay half-life 60 games, preseason prior), take the posterior covariance of (attack_A+defence_B)+(attack_B+defence_A) per game, add the playoff_context and league_scoring_environment multiplier SDs, and express as SD of expected goals per game as of the pre-series timestamp; draw one value per simulated series. Validate by comparing the PIT of observed series totals 2005-06 onward with and without the shared term.
free_sources: Own computation from MoneyPuck free CSVs and NHL API game results
Natural Stat Trick team splits (free scrape)
raw_data: team-game goals and xG for and against by strength state
playoff game results with series id
nhl.series_pair_scoring_rate_uncertainty.why: Sets the width of the series total-goals distribution beyond per-game overdispersion, which decides tail strikes such as 50+ goals.

nhl.series_context.reason: State of the series (games played, goals banked so far, home sequence) is exactly the conditioning information for a live total; before the series it supplies the home-ice sequence.

nhl.ratings.reason: Drives per-game win probability, which sets the length distribution; the rating gap is the main reason a series total depends on the pair.

nhl.goalie_quality.reason: Playoff goals are largely a function of goalies; goals saved above expected feeds both goal mean and the chance of lopsided games.

nhl.total_goal_dispersion.reason: Per-game variance and home/away correlation; its catalog label includes empty-net goals, so when the explicit empty_net module is active the dispersion is fitted on non-empty-net goals to avoid double counting.

nhl.playoff_context.reason: Playoff environment (tighter benches, fewer penalties, sudden-death OT) shifts the goal mean below regular-season levels; it also indicates OT format.

nhl.xg_for.reason: Process-based scoring measure; partially overlaps with ratings, so it adds mainly by separating shot quality from finishing.

nhl.xg_against.reason: Same as xg_for for the defensive side; useful but correlated with goalie quality in how it is measured.

nhl.series_goalie_volatility.reason: Goalie performance clusters within series; widens the goal total and changes length in a direction that depends on whether the favourite's or underdog's goalie runs hot.

nhl.pace.reason: Attempt volume sets scoring chances; playoff pace differs from regular season so it needs playoff weighting.

nhl.special_teams.reason: Power-play opportunities are fewer in the playoffs but conversion matters; moderate contribution to goal mean.

nhl.penalty_rates.reason: Penalty counts feed power-play goal chances, but referee crews in the playoffs call fewer, lessening the effect.

nhl.injuries_pit.reason: Matters when a star or starting goalie is out; frequency per series is lowish, so secondary rather than primary for totals.

nhl.empty_net.reason: Explicit state-conditional empty-net module for elimination and one-goal states; kept only with total_goal_dispersion refitted net of empty-net goals, otherwise drop as duplicate.

nhl.league_scoring_environment.reason: Calibrates the level of goals per game by season; shifts the mean but does not differentiate series.

nhl.reg_tie_model.reason: Regulation-tie probability is the rate of OT games, hence of the +1 sudden-death goal in totals and the per-game rate for the OT-count contract. Must be computed from the own bivariate goal model (market_dependency: hybrid_rebuild); calibration buckets use own-model expected total and margin, never posted totals, spreads or regulation-winner prices.

nhl.series_ot_count_dependence.reason: Beta-binomial overdispersion of OT-game counts directly sets the tail for KXNHLSERIESOT strikes like 'at least 5 games go to overtime'.

nhl.rating_posterior_uncertainty.reason: Shared uncertainty in the pair's strength differential shortens expected length and shifts winner-by-length cells when integrated over; its catalog definition (xG/goal differential state-space) does not carry total-scoring-level uncertainty, which is the separate new input series_pair_scoring_rate_uncertainty.

nhl.goalie_start_forecast.reason: Playoff starter changes are rarer than in the regular season but decisive when they happen; its back-to-back rotation logic mostly does not apply in playoffs.

nhl.rest_travel.reason: Rest between playoff games ranges from one to three or more days and cross-country travel occurs within series; modest per-game effect.

nhl.bracket_path_difficulty.reason: Only needed for markets listed before the matchup is fixed (championship score) and for the league-wide 0-3 comeback event.

interactions.mechanism: Expected length and P(game 7) are concave in per-game win probability near parity, so integrating over the strength-differential posterior lowers both and moves mass to sweeps and five-game series.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare predicted game-7 and sweep shares from point ratings vs posterior draws on 2005-06 onward series, by log-loss bucketed by pre-series rating gap.

interactions.mechanism: A hot favourite goalie both shortens the series and lowers goals per game, so both channels cut the total; a hot underdog goalie lowers goals per game but lengthens the series, so the channels offset. The interaction is conditional on which side's goalie deviates.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress series total and length on favourite-goalie and underdog-goalie in-series GSAx separately and test opposite signs on length.

interactions.mechanism: Empty-net goals are rare in neutral states but common when a team trails by one late in an elimination game; the empty-net contribution to goals is concentrated in the elimination states, so its effect depends on series state.
interactions.how_to_test: Tabulate empty-net goals per game by series state and elimination flag and test the interaction in a Poisson regression.

interactions.mechanism: OT-game count is beta-binomial over games played with per-game rate from the tie model; evenly matched pairs have higher tie rates and longer series at once, so the upper tail of the count (5+ OT games) rises much faster than either factor alone.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare observed OT-count distribution of 2005-06 onward series with independent-length vs joint-length simulations, bucketed by pre-series rating gap.

interactions.mechanism: Early games reflect the regular-season matchup, while later games reflect adjustment and heavier playoff structure (fewer penalties, tighter checking); scoring drifts between regimes by game index.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit goals per game by game index with round fixed effects and test a break between games 1-3 and 4-7.

interactions.mechanism: A 0-3 comeback is four consecutive wins by the trailing team: the per-game state-shifted win rate is raised to the fourth power, and any bounce-back dependence multiplies each step, so small shifts compound strongly.
interactions.how_to_test: Predict the count of 0-3 comebacks and of 0-3 to 3-3 recoveries over 1987-2026 with and without state shift and dependence terms; compare with observed counts.

interactions.mechanism: The shared scoring-level error enters every game, so its contribution to the variance of series goals is its variance times games squared; length is longest for evenly rated pairs, so the same uncertainty widens total-goal tails far more for close matchups than for mismatches.
interactions.how_to_test: Bucket 2005-06 onward series by pre-series rating gap and compare the variance of series total goals against a per-game-only model and a model adding the shared term; check PIT of totals by bucket.

nonlinearities.shape: Expected series length rises concavely as per-game win probability approaches 50 percent, reaching 5.8125 games at iid parity
nonlinearities.why: The mean of a best-of-seven saturates near parity and falls quickly as one team becomes a heavy favourite, so goals scale concavely with team balance.

nonlinearities.shape: Effect on goals against is roughly linear for ordinary goalies but compresses at the top because shot quality limits how much any goalie can save
nonlinearities.why: Goals saved above expected measured on regular-season shots tends to regress strongly in playoffs; extreme values are shrunk heavily, which makes the effect saturating.

nonlinearities.shape: Series total = regulation goals + number of tied games: each tie adds a deterministic +1, a step that interacts with integer strikes
nonlinearities.why: With sudden-death OT the period count is irrelevant; only P(tie) per game moves the total, and near an integer strike one extra OT game flips settlement.

nonlinearities.shape: Comeback probability scales as the fourth power of the trailing team's per-game win rate
nonlinearities.why: Four consecutive wins are required, so a 0.05 change in per-game probability around 0.45 moves the comeback probability by roughly 40 percent relative.
